_comment: The status-check contexts that BLOCK a merge to main. Mirror of GitHub
repo ruleset 23605458 'main: PR + required checks', read back 2026-09-25
(read-only GETs, org on the Team plan): enforcement: active, target
~DEFAULT_BRANCH, no bypass actors. Its rules: deletion and
non_fast_forward (main cannot be deleted or force-pushed), pull_request
(no direct push to main; zero approvals required), and
required_status_checks on exactly the contexts below (integration_id
15368, GitHub Actions) with strict_required_status_checks_policy: false
(`strict` below; it was true only 2026-09-23 15:39Z-20:50Z, ruleset
history v50656329 -> v50691329). So a PR can merge while behind main:
its checks ran on its merge with an older main, not on the tree that
lands. What verifies that tree before any image is published is the
ci.yml call in build-push-ghcr.yml on the push to main.
This file is the source of truth for scripts/check-required-checks.mjs,
which runs on every PR (npm run lint:checks). Keep it and the ruleset in
step: a context added here but not there is checked by nobody on GitHub,
one added there but not here is not checked for uniqueness. Refresh the
`ruleset` block (read-only GET, starts no Action) with:
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $GH_TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
https://api.github.com/repos/Bee-Flow/Bee-Flow-AI/rulesets/23605458
BEFORE ADDING A CONTEXT HERE, read what the checker enforces. A context is
only safe to require if exactly one job emits it, that job is not a matrix,
its workflow has a pull_request trigger, that trigger has NO paths: filter,
and the job is unconditional or an `if: always()` aggregate that needs
every other job in its workflow.
`checks-passed` is ci.yml's aggregate: every test and lint job lives in
that one workflow, path-filtered per job (not at the trigger), and the
aggregate runs always and fails if any job that ran failed. That is what
lets a single context gate server, frontend, mobile, Python, guard and
Nextcloud tests without blocking a docs-only PR.
